scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Your phone is silent, yet it buzzes in your pocket. What's moving inside a solid phone?

scenes.name: erm
scenes.text: Older phones use a tiny motor with an off-centre weight. As it spins, the uneven weight shakes the phone.

scenes.name: lra
scenes.text: Many newer phones use a linear motor instead. A small magnet and mass slide back and forth on a spring.

scenes.name: coil
scenes.text: A coil becomes an electromagnet when current flows, pushing and pulling the magnet many times a second.

scenes.name: haptics
scenes.text: Because the linear motor starts and stops quickly, it can create crisp taps and clicks. That's called haptic feedback.

scenes.name: patterns
scenes.text: Software controls timing and strength, so a call, a message and a keyboard tap can each feel different.

scenes.name: battery
scenes.text: Vibration uses a bit more battery than a quiet notification, but far less than the screen.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: A moving mass, pushed by a magnet. Follow for more on how things really work.
